value.text: The file is a summary of the Constitution of the United States, outlining its structure and key powers. Main Points: • [1] The document establishes the U.S. Constitution, which forms a federal government with two houses: the House of Representatives (members chosen every two years based on state population) and the Senate (elected by legislatures for six-year terms). Both houses must meet annually at least once in December unless designated otherwise. • [2] Bills requiring passage from both houses must be presented to the President; if signed, they become law. If not signed within ten days (excluding Sundays), they take effect automatically unless Congress adjourns. Resolutions needing concurrence from both houses require presidential approval or a two-thirds vote in each chamber before taking effect. • [3] The Constitution creates a three-branch system: the President holds executive power, the Supreme Court holds judicial power, and Congress is responsible for approving treaties and federal laws (which are supreme over state laws). It also mandates that all taxes be paid into the federal Treasury under congressional supervision. • [4] Federal law and treaties take precedence over state laws. The Constitution requires a three-fourths majority of states to approve any amendments, ensuring their authority remains supreme. Summary of all 9 pages.
